children.text: Junior year is the last year a student can actually build their application since senior year can only describe it. Join Brennan, a former UC Berkeley admissions officer and Stanford reader, for a practical breakdown of exactly what needs to happen this year to walk into senior fall ready instead of scrambling. You'll learn how to sequence testing so it's finished before applications open, how to turn activities from involvement into real leadership, and which academic decisions actually move the needle with a reader. Brennan will also cover the timing mistakes that quietly cost students options they don't find out about until it's too late to fix them. Whether your student is just starting junior year or already behind, this session gives you a clear plan instead of a checklist off the internet.
In this webinar, you'll learn:
The Clock That Actually Matters:
Senior fall is for describing, not building. Brennan breaks down what has to be finished by the end of junior year to make that possible.
Testing Done Early Buys Freedom:
Students who finish testing by junior spring get a senior fall built around essays and applications — not test prep.
Leadership Isn't a Title:
Readers score initiative and results, not the word on a name badge. Learn what actually counts as leadership in a reader's eyes.

meta.description: Most families think a prestigious summer program name is what impresses admissions officers at top colleges.

children.text: Most families think a prestigious summer program name is what impresses admissions officers. It's not, and chasing the wrong programs can actually work against strong students. Join Ben, a former admissions officer at Vanderbilt and Johns Hopkins, for a candid look at what selective summer programs actually signal to a reader and where families waste time and money chasing the wrong ones. You'll learn how admissions officers actually evaluate summer activities, why a $10,000 pre-college program often reads no better than a self-directed project, and how to choose or design a summer experience that reinforces the story your student is already telling. Whether your student hasn't planned their summer yet or already has offers in hand, this session will help you make the choice that actually moves the needle.
In this webinar, you'll learn:
What "Prestigious" Actually Signals:
A big-name program logo doesn't carry the weight families think it does. Ben breaks down what readers really look for in a summer activity, and it's rarely the brand.
The Expensive Program Trap:
Paying for access isn't the same as building depth. Learn why self-directed or lower-cost summers often outperform costly "pre-college" programs on an application.
Making It Fit the Story:
The best summer activities connect to something bigger in a student's narrative. Get a framework for choosing a summer that strengthens—not distracts from—their overall application.

Cassidy walks families through exactly what should (and shouldn't) happen in 10th grade, so students aren't scrambling to catch up later.

children.text: Sophomore year feels early, but it's often the last real window for students to build the foundation that makes the rest of high school manageable. Join Cassidy for, Former Admissions Director at UCSD, for a practical session on what 10th graders should actually be focusing on academically, extracurricularly, and in early college planning. You'll learn which decisions made now quietly shape junior and senior year options, where families over- or under-prioritize their time, and how to set a realistic, personalized plan instead of reacting to what other families are doing. Whether your student is coasting or already anxious about "falling behind," this session will help you build a clear, confident game plan for the two years ahead.
In this webinar, you'll learn:
The Decisions That Compound:
Some choices made sophomore year—course selection, activity commitments—quietly narrow or widen options later. Learn which ones actually matter long-term.
Balance Over Burnout:
Trying to do everything early often backfires. Cassidy breaks down how to prioritize depth and sustainability over a packed sophomore-year resume.
A Plan, Not a Panic:
Every student's timeline looks different. Get a framework for building a personalized sophomore-year plan instead of comparing your student to everyone else's.
